reason: The hypothesis makes multiple specific claims about the formation, composition, properties, and performance of a ZrTiO4 oxide layer on an AlCrTiZrMo HEA film, but cites no prior evidence whatsoever to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific oxidation behavior of this alloy or the tribo-corrosion performance of such a layer.
premises: Thermal annealing of AlCrTiZrMo HEA film at 800 °C in air forms a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer
The ZrTiO4 oxide layer is robust, adherent, and resists mechanical spallation during sliding
The oxide layer acts as a physical barrier that limits corrosive ingress
An intact oxide layer decouples wear and corrosion, reducing synergistic degradation
In situ monitoring can track oxide layer integrity and correlate it with tribo-corrosion response
